intro: Open the app, check the shape, and make a photo or a video from one photo or a product link. A video can include a spoken line, an AI actor, a voice, captions, and music.

faq.q: Which app should I make a file for first?
faq.a: Start with the app that already gets your orders. Make that shape and post it. If you also sell somewhere else, make a second shape from the same photo.

faq.q: Can one tall video run in more than one full-screen spot?
faq.a: A 9:16 video is the tall shape those full-screen spots share. You make that file once. You can send it to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram), or download it and upload it in each ad account. Check each app's file rules before you run the ad.

faq.q: What shape should a photo in the post list use?
faq.a: Use a square photo. Photos from this tool are square. It does not make a 4:5 photo, or a 4:3 or 3:4 photo. Videos can be 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4. If the app wants 4:5, crop the square photo in your editor, then upload it.

faq.q: How long can a video be?
faq.a: You can pick 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Credits are the points a file spends. A 6-second video is 24 credits, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. You see the cost before you start. If it fails, the credits come back.

faq.q: What should I make for a marketplace listing?
faq.a: Start with a square photo on a plain background for the main image. Then add a detail photo or a lifestyle photo. A video is optional. It usually sits beside the photos, not in the main image slot.

faq.q: What should a store gallery use?
faq.a: Keep the gallery photos square so the grid lines up. Add a short video when motion explains the product better than another photo.

faq.q: Can you publish the file to my ad account?
faq.a: You can send the finished file to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram) in one click. You can also download it. You still set who sees it, the budget, and the schedule in the ad account. Type the price so it matches your store now.

faq.q: Can one file run on every app unchanged?
faq.a: The product can stay the same. The shape usually should not. A square listing photo and a tall 9:16 video are two files from one photo.

faq.q: How do I keep the product off the app's buttons?
faq.a: Leave space around the product in a tall 9:16 video. Check the file on a phone before you pay for ads. The button layout is different on each app.

faq.q: Do I need a separate video for every app?
faq.a: Make a separate file when the shape changes. Two apps that both take a tall 9:16 video can use the same download if their file rules match.

faq.q: Can I use the download in paid ads?
faq.a: Yes. You can use finished files for your shop, and they have no watermark. Music can come from the library. You are responsible for what the spoken line says.
Captions are written on the video. Edit them in the editor on this site so the price matches your store now. You can still change the post text in the ad account.

faq.q: Can one batch cover more than one app?
faq.a: Yes. A batch is several files from the same photo. Run one when the shape changes. Two apps that both take a tall 9:16 video can share one download if their file rules match. Each file shows its credit cost.

faq.q: Does the video include a voice?
faq.a: Yes, when you write a line and pick an AI actor or a voice. The speech is made by AI. It is not a customer review.

faq.q: Can my own tools start a file for an app?
faq.a: Yes. An API lets your other software start a photo or video here. The credit cost is the same as on this site.

benefits.d: Describe the product and the app. The tool writes the spoken line, and you edit it.
Use an actor when you do not want to be on camera. The person is made by AI, not a real customer.
Put a song under the video and swap it in the editor.
Captions come on the file. Change them so the price matches your store now.
Paste a public product page. Its main image and name start the video for this app.
Photos are square. A video can be 9:16 (tall), 1:1 (square), 16:9 (wide), 4:3, or 3:4, at 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.

more_sections.lead: Eight kinds of post. Use the one that fits the app, and keep the product easy to recognize.

items.d: A short action people can copy, with your product, for a full-screen post.
One useful step, spoken and captioned, so the action is easy to follow.
A single everyday moment with the item, not a long plot.
An AI actor responds to one real detail, such as the texture or the sound.
Two or three real features, each on screen long enough to read.
The package, the material, or the setup, from the photo you uploaded.
The item, held simply, with light music and few words.
An AI actor in a brief scene that ends on the product.

A photo is 24 credits. A video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. You see that cost before it starts.
